title: When the Spire Falls Revisited
premise: Oscar Amberdale, a temple scribe indentured by her father's debts, has survived Thornfell by knowing every smuggler's path and keeping her head down—until a mute child arrives speaking the dead tongue of the Spire, the fortress whose fall ended the old war. The child's words are a map to the Spire's buried heart, and both the temple and a resurgent order of zealots will kill to claim it. As the thirteenth moon waxes, Oscar must choose between erasing the child to save herself or carrying the secret through the mountains to the last living heir of the fallen Spire. She delivers the child, pays her debt with the only coin that matters—the truth of her own Spire-blood inheritance—and watches the secret be buried rather than weaponized, at the cost of the life she knew.
about_author: P. M. Vane is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated manuscripts in a mountain monastery before turning to fiction. They write about people who carry dangerous knowledge in places where knowledge is contraband.

chapters.title: The Debt of Ink
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. We meet Oscar copying penance-ledgers in the temple of Vess, chafing under her inherited debt, when a starving child appears at the scriptorium door speaking a language no living scholar claims—and Oscar realizes, with cold dread, that she can half-understand it. Emotional beat: the uneasy recognition that her carefully small life has just cracked open.

chapters.title: Thirteen Moons
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, with an interlude from the zealot captain Rell. Deciphering the child's words reveals a map to the Spire's heart and a deadline: the thirteenth moon. When the temple's abbot demands the child as 'evidence,' Oscar flees with her into the smuggler roads she knows best, hunted by both church and zealots. Emotional beat: fear hardening into fierce protectiveness.

chapters.title: What the Mountain Remembers
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. In the high passes, the child speaks her first clear word—Oscar's own name in the old tongue—and Oscar confronts why she understood it: her family's blood runs back to the Spire's defenders. Ambushed by Rell's zealots, she survives by collapsing a smuggler's bridge, losing their supplies and nearly the child. Emotional beat: grief for the self she was, acceptance of what she carries.

chapters.title: The Falling Place
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. At the buried heart of the Spire they find the last heir, an old woman guarding not a weapon but a choice: reignite the war or let the bloodline end quietly. Oscar argues for burial; Rell arrives to force ignition, and the heir dies holding the door. Oscar seals the heart with the child inside its protection, her debt transmuted into guardianship. Emotional beat: sorrowful peace—survival paid for, love chosen over duty.
